newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Petronas considering further Iran energy projects.
newsitem.headline: Petronas considering further Iran energy projects.

text.p: Malaysian state-oil firm Petronas is considering further energy investments in Iran despite the threat of U.S. trade sanctions, Petronas president Dato Mohamed Hassan Marican said on Tuesday.

"We continue to talk and explore further opportunities (in Iran) like many companies...We are looking at many potential projects," Marican told reporters on the sidelines of an energy conference in Abu Dhabi.

Petronas has linked up with France's Total SA to develop Iran's Sirri E and A offshore oil and gas fields in a development which represented the biggest direct foreign investment in Iran's energy industry since its 1979 revolution.

U.S. President Bill Clinton signed the Iran-Libya Sanctions Act last year which gave the president powers to impose a range of sanctions against non-U.S. firms that invested $40 million or more a year in the two countries' oil and gas sectors.
Petronas did not expect U.S. sanctions to be imposed against it for the multi-million dollar investment in Sirri.
"Sirri development is not covered under the sanctions...that bridge has been crossed," said Marican.

Marican would not elaborate on which specific Iranian projects the company was looking at but industry sources say the Malaysian entity is looking to join an international consortium to further develop the giant South Pars gas field.
It has also been linked with developing at least one more Iranian offshore oil and gas field.

Marican also stated that Petronas this week had joined a Chinese-U.S. consortium to carry out exploration work in Sudan and that other countries including Iraq and Burma were also being eyed as future potential investment opportunities.
Output from Petronas' acreage in Syria, the first overseas production for the company, would start in July, he added.
